## Structure and components

- [statement] Preproduction includes checking whether the specified cards and components can be manufactured and reviewing proof prints; Cartamundi explicitly includes these activities in its service. (low confidence) — https://cartamundi.com/en/cardgame-boardgame-solutions/ · keywords: Playing-card print production systems

## How it works

- [statement] LongPack’s preproduction-card documentation warns of stock substitution, color differences and omitted varnish in its digital sample process. These are limitations of that documented sample route, not proof that every digital production press has those limitations. (low confidence) — https://help.longpackgames.com/article/105-08-cards · keywords: Playing-card print production systems
- [statement] Smartpress advises against Soft Touch laminate for playing cards because it can impede shuffling. A finish marketed for tactile appeal should therefore be checked on a playable sample before selection. (low confidence) — https://smartpress.com/support/product-faq/collated-printing-faq · keywords: Playing-card print production systems
- [statement] Shuffled Ink recommends a hard-copy proof when print color is a concern and does not guarantee an exact color match across a production run. Digital artwork approval alone should not be treated as physical color acceptance. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://shuffledink.com/terms-and-conditions · keywords: Playing-card print production systems

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] PrintNinja describes linen texture as a mechanical embossing step on printed parent sheets before cutting; texture therefore cannot be specified solely by the print engine’s image resolution. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/card-game-production/ · keywords: Playing-card print production systems

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Koehler describes applying a dedicated playing-card varnish over printed ink. Its process explanation treats printed paper alone as insufficient for easy handling; this supports evaluating the finished coating rather than treating image reproduction as a shuffle-quality test. (low confidence) — https://www.koehlerpaper.com/en/news/publications/Customers-have-a-winning-hand-with-Koehler-cardboard.php · keywords: Playing-card print production systems

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A complete paper-card production system extends beyond the print engine: printing is followed by converting sheets into cards, assembling complete decks and packaging them. (medium confidence) — https://www.madehow.com/Volume-4/Playing-Cards.html · keywords: Playing-card print production systems · also: https://printninja.com/card-game-production/
- [statement] MPC describes digital production-line printing for small quantities and offset printing for large quantities; this establishes two paper-card production routes without establishing a universal volume crossover. (low confidence) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/pops/card-print-types.html · keywords: Playing-card print production systems
- [statement] Printed imagery and card surface treatment are separate operations: the manufacturing reference describes protective polymer coating after printing, while LongPack distinguishes its unvarnished samples from mass-production cards with Poker varnish. (medium confidence) — https://www.madehow.com/Volume-4/Playing-Cards.html · keywords: Playing-card print production systems · also: https://help.longpackgames.com/article/105-08-cards
- [statement] PrintNinja describes alternative converting routes: its domestic rotary die cutter trims card size and rounded corners together, while another described route rounds and smooths previously trimmed card stacks in a separate operation. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/card-game-production/ · keywords: Playing-card print production systems
- [statement] Deck assembly depends on sheet layout and sorting as well as cutting: PrintNinja imposes cards in assembly order so collation occurs during trimming; Cartamundi France describes cutting sheets into strips and cards, then sorting and packaging the cards. (medium confidence) — https://printninja.com/card-game-production/ · keywords: Playing-card print production systems · also: https://cartamundi.fr/fr/services/production/carte-et-emballage/
- [statement] Duplo describes the DC-618 as a finisher for digitally printed sheets that slits, cuts, creases and perforates. Its speed specification is in sheets per minute; that specification alone does not establish completed playing-card decks per hour. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-618-slitter-cutter-creaser/ · keywords: Playing-card print production systems
- [statement] Quality control spans more than image appearance: the manufacturing reference describes incoming-material checks, removal of defective printed sheets before cutting and line inspections during production. (low confidence) — https://www.madehow.com/Volume-4/Playing-Cards.html · keywords: Playing-card print production systems
- [statement] A finished paper-card deck requires production beyond the print engine: manufacturers describe coating, cutting, corner rounding, collation and packing, with artwork/specification review before production and checks afterward. This is a workflow map, not proof that one printer performs every stage. (medium confidence) — https://www.apexplayingcards.com/factory · keywords: Playing-card print production systems · also: https://printninja.com/card-game-production/
- [statement] MPC describes digital printing for small card quantities and offset printing for large quantities; its description gives no universal quantity at which ownership or offset becomes economical. (low confidence) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/pops/card-print-types.html · keywords: Playing-card print production systems
- [statement] PrintNinja describes arranging cards on parent sheets so trimming also collates the deck. For repeated identical games, sheet layout and deck assembly therefore need to be planned together; separate manual sorting is not inherent to every workflow. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/card-game-production/ · keywords: Playing-card print production systems
- [statement] Cartamundi describes its casino-card quality controls as extending from prepress to packaging, using counting, weight and vision checks. These are manufacturer-described controls, not an independently measured defect rate for a proposed game production line. (low confidence) — https://cartamundi.asia/en/cases/casino-playing-cards/ · keywords: Playing-card print production systems
- [statement] Smartpress says collated sets can ship unseparated if neither stapling nor shrink wrapping is selected. Collation and individually bundled game sets are separate order requirements. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://smartpress.com/support/product-faq/collated-printing-faq · keywords: Playing-card print production systems
- [statement] Duplo states that the CC-229 cuts up to 130 business cards per minute. That application-specific cutter rating is not evidence of a completed playing-card-deck production rate. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/cc-229-card-cutter/ · keywords: Playing-card print production systems
